entries.title: CHEST: LATERAL
entries.notes:
14x17 LW       SID: 72" 
CR: ⟂ to MCP at T7
Breath: Suspend at end of 2nd full inspiration

Top of IR: 1.5-2” above shoulders
Collimation: 1" border around skin line

Position: Rest arms above head or hold bar (IV stand in front)

Notes: Left Lateral preferred

entries.title: CHEST: PA Upright
entries.notes:
14x17 CW or LW      SID: 72" 
CR: ⟂ to MSP at T7
Breath: Suspend at end of 2nd full inspiration

IR Top: 1.5-2” above shoulders
Collimation: 1" border around skin line

Position: 

Chin extended slightly
Back of hands low on hips or grabbing bars on IR
Roll shoulders forward

entries.title: CHEST: LATERAL DECUBITUS
entries.notes:
14x17 LW      SID: 72" 
CR: Horizontal & ⟂ to GRID; 
       3" below jugular notch for AP;
       T7 for PA
Breath: Suspend at end of 2nd full inspiration

IR Top: 1.5-2” above shoulders
Collimation: 14x17

Position: 

Extend arms over head
Adjust thorax to true lateral
Elevate body 2-3" off table with sponge

Notes: Left lateral decubitus preferred

entries.title: C-Spine: AP ODONTOID (Open-Mouth) C1-C2
entries.notes:
10x12 LW      SID: 30" 
CR: ⟂ to IR; Enters midpoint of the open mouth
Breath: “AHH” softly during exposure (brings tongue down)

Collimation: 5x5

Position: 

Open mouth & adjust head so lower surface of upper incisors to tips of mastoid ⟂ to IR
Mouth open as wide as possible
(Shows Atlas: C1 & Axis: C2)

entries.title: C-Spine: AP AXIAL OBLIQUE (LPO/RPO)
entries.notes:
10x12 LW      SID: 72" 
CR: 15-20° cephalad, directed to C4 
Breath: Suspend

Collimation: 10x12 
IR: Centered to C3 body
      1" superior to most prominent point of thyroid cartilage

Position: 

Rotate shoulders 45° & center to cervical spine to IR
Elevate & protrude chin
(Shows intervertebral foramina and pedicles farthest from the IR)

Notes: LPO = right foramina | RPO = left foramina

entries.title: C-Spine: LATERAL (GRANDY)
entries.notes:
10x12 LW      SID: 72" 
CR: Horizontal & ⟂ to MCP at C4
Breath: Suspend at end of full expiration

Collimation: 10x12 
Top of IR: 1” above top of EAM
  
Position: 

Sandbags to patient's wrists to depress shoulders (to get C7)
C4 in center
Elevate chin slightly, mandible protruded
(Shows vertebral bodies, zygapophyseal joints, & open intervertebral disk spaces)

Notes: *If cervical spine trauma is suspected, this projection must be performed first and *cleared* by radiologist before additional images are performed.


*If top third of T1 is not demonstrated, lateral of cervicothoracic is required (Swimmers).

entries.title: C-Spine: AP DENS (FUCHS)
entries.notes:
10x12 CW      SID: 40" 
CR: ⟂ to IR; Enters the neck on the MSP just distal to the tip of the chin
Breath: Suspend

Collimation: 5x5

Position: 

Center the IR to the level of the tips of the mastoid processes
Extend the chin until the tip of the chin and the tips of the mastoid process are vertical
Adjust the head so that the MSP is perpendicular to the plane of the grid
(Shows dens within the foramen magnum)

Notes: Fuchs method is contraindicated if cervical fracture or disease is suspected.

entries.title: C-Spine: LATERAL - Hyperflexion & Hyperextension
tags: hyperextension; c-spine lateral hyperextension; c-spine lateral hyperflexion
entries.notes:
10x12 LW      SID: 72" 
CR: Horizontal & ⟂ to C4
Breath: Suspend 

Collimation: 10x12 
Top of IR: 1” above top of EAM
  
Position: 

Same as for lateral (Grandy)
Hyperflexion: Have patient drop head forward and draw the chin as close as possible to chest; Body of the mandible almost vertical

Hyperextension: Have patient elevate chin and relax head as far back as possible; Body of the mandible almost horizontal

Elevate chin slightly, mandible protruded
(Checks for absent motion from trauma/disease)

Notes: *Used to demonstrate absence of normal movement from trauma or disease.
*This procedure must not be attempted until cervical spine pathology or fracture has been ruled out.

entries.title: C-Spine: PA AXIAL OBLIQUE (RAO/LAO) *preferred*
entries.notes:
10x12 LW      SID: 72" 
CR: 15-20° caudad, Directed to C4 
Breath: Suspend

Collimation: 10x12 
IR: Centered to C5 body
      1" caudal to most prominent point of thyroid cartilage

Position: 

Rotate body & neck 45° 
Center cervical spine to IR
Elevate & protrude chin
(Shows RAO/LAO = Intervertebral foramina and pedicles closest to the IR)

Notes: RAO = right foramina | LAO = left foramina

entries.title: T-Spine: AP
entries.notes:
14x17 LW      SID: 40" 
CR: ⟂ to IR; ½ between jugular notch & xiphoid (T7)
Breath: Suspend at full expiration

Collimation: 7x17
Top of IR: 1.5-2” above shoulders (this places T7 in center) 

Position: 

MSP centered to grid
If supine, reduce kyphosis by flexing hips and knees to place thighs vertical
If upright, weight should be equally distributed on both feet
(Shows costovertebral articulations)

Notes: If possible, orient patient so lower thorax is at cathode end of x-ray tube. This orientation takes advantage of the “anode heel effect” to ensure a more uniform exposure of the thoracic anatomy.

entries.title: SCOLIOSIS: LATERAL ThoracoLumbar Spine
entries.notes:
14x17 LW      SID: 40-72”
CR: ⟂ to IR

Centering points for each sequence will be dictated by the system used
A two (or three) image sequence is performed 
Breath: Suspend 

Collimation: varies

Position: 

MSP parallel with the IR
MCP perpendicular to midline of grid
Arms at right angle to body or upward 
Position special ruler adjacent to spine, if needed
(shows entire spine from base of skull to tip of coccyx)

entries.title: CervicoThoracic Spine: LATERAL (SWIMMERS)
entries.notes:
10x12 LW      SID: 40"
CR: ⟂ to C7-T1 interspace (if shoulder away from IR is depressed)
If shoulder cannot be depressed, angle 3 to 5° caudad (to better visualize the C7-T1 articulation)
Breath: Suspend or use a breathing technique (to blur lung anatomy)

Collimation: 10x12
Top of IR: 1.5-2” above relaxed shoulders

Position: 

MCP centered to midline of grid
Extend arm closer to IR above head, and rotate humeral head anteriorly (If upright, flex elbow, and rest forearm on head)
Depress shoulder farther from IR (If possible, rotate humeral head in the opposite direction to the other shoulder)
Head and body in true lateral position
C7-T1 interspace in center 
(shows upper thoracic because it tends to be very dense)

Notes: The swimmer’s technique is performed when shoulder superimposition obscures C7 on a lateral cervical spine projection or when a lateral projection of the upper thoracic vertebra is needed.

entries.title: T-Spine: LATERAL
entries.notes:
14x17 LW      SID: 48” or greater to reduce magnification 
CR: ⟂ to posterior half of thorax at T7 (if spine is horizontal)
       10-15° cephalad if spine is not horizontal
Breath: Breathing normal or Suspend at full expiration or Breathing technique (an increase        exposure time, 2-3 seconds with corresponding decrease in mA)

Collimation: 7x17
Top of IR: 1.5-2” above relaxed shoulders 

Position: 

Long axis of vertebral column aligned horizontal (Firm support for head and lower portion, if needed)
Superimpose hips and knees for true lateral position 
Center the posterior half of the thorax to the midline of the grid and at the level of T7

Adjust arms to right angle from body
Place a sheet of lead on the table, behind the patient (Absorbs scatter radiation; Prevents table scatter from affecting the image)

(Shows intervertebral foramina of the thoracic spine)

Notes: T1 to T3 are not well seen. SI of the shoulders on the upper vertebrae may cause underexposure in this area. The number of vertebrae visualized depends on the size and shape of the patient.

entries.title: C-Spine: AP AXIAL
entries.notes:
10x12 LW      SID: 40" 
CR: 15-20° cephalic; MSP at C4 
(Enters at or slightly inferior to the Adam’s apple)
Breath: Suspend

Collimation: 10” LW & 1” outside skin line on sides
IR: Top of ears

Position: 

Extend chin so occlusal plane is ⟂ to IR
C4 in center of IR
Shoulders in same plane
(Shows C3–T2 bodies & open intervertebral disk spaces)

Notes: Provide support for the head of any patient who has a pronounced lordotic curvature. (Helps compensate for the curvature and reduces image distortion)

entries.title: CHEST: AP Supine
entries.notes:
14x17  LW      SID: 72" 
CR: ⟂ to long axis of sternum; ⟂ to center of IR; 
        3” below jugular notch
Breath: Suspend at end of 2nd full inspiration

IR Top: 1.5-2” above relaxed shoulders
Collimation: 14x17

Position: 

Center MSP to IR
Flex elbows; pronate hands; Place hands on hips to draw scapula laterally

Elevate head with support sponge
